extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting preprints to EarthArXiv (authors in Earth & Planetary Science)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and moderation criteria for preparing and submitting preprints or postprints to EarthArXiv, including scope, required metadata and files, acceptable/ unacceptable content types, and policies on plagiarism, withdrawals, name changes, and licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: relevant to Earth and Planetary Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Your paper is of interest to the Earth and Planetary Science community. Submissions related to Astronomy and Space Physics are outside the scope of EarthArXiv. Submissions related to Environmental Biology and Ecology with an Earth or Planetary Science perspective are welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your paper is outside the scope of EarthArXiv, consider submitting to other preprint servers (e.g., arXiv, agriRxiv, bioRxiv, EcoEvoRxiv, paleorXiv, MarXiv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required manuscript elements (title, abstract, authors, affiliations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your paper contains a title, abstract, author names, and affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these elements are present in the submitted PDF and in the metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter must be an author listed on the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv will only accept submissions that have been uploaded by one of the authors listed on the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions from anyone not listed as an author will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete metadata (all authors, at least one keyword)
rubrics_metrics.description: All EarthArXiv metadata must be provided. For example, all authors listed on the paper must appear in the metadata, and at least one keyword must be selected for indexing purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full author lists and select keywords to ensure proper indexing and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper must be written in English, as we cannot guarantee moderation of the content of non-English manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-English manuscripts are not supported for moderation; translate before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and single-PDF requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit your paper in PDF format. Do not submit additional PDFs with supplemental material. All material must be included in ONE PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a short appendix in a separate file, you must combine these into one file prior to submission. EarthArXiv does not host other supplementary materials directly but allows links to external repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author email required
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one author must supply an email address for correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correspondence email is included in the PDF and matches metadata where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement and matching email
rubrics_metrics.description: The author/submitter will include a full URL link to their ORCID account on the coversheet or at the top of the first page of the submission. The ORCID information must include educational history and current or recent work affiliations. The ORCID email address must match the submitter's email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ORCID registration link if you do not have an ORCID. Place the ORCID URL on the coversheet or first page as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-peer-reviewed or postprint statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: Your paper clearly states that this is a non-peer reviewed preprint submitted to EarthArXiv, or a post print of a published manuscript with the journal name and DOI clearly indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may (Option 1) include a cover sheet with the statement and journal name/DOI or (Option 2) include a header on each page identifying the paper as a non-peer reviewed EarthArXiv preprint or as a postprint. Upon submission you will be asked to check a box confirming that a cover sheet was included; if you check the box but still do not include a cover page, moderators may prepend a basic statement to your submission and you can later revise by submitting a newer version. Templates are available in the resources page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials policy and external repository recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv does not host other supplementary materials directly. During preprint submission, EarthArXiv provides options for authors to include links to external sites, which will be displayed alongside the published preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to use free hosting sites such as GitHub, Zenodo, and FigShare for software, research notebooks, small datasets, and related supplementary materials. When intending to supplement a preprint with software, collections of files, and/or an extensive Appendix of tables or figures, authors are encouraged to set up an external repository prior to submission. Moderators will work with authors on a case-by-case basis when the distinction between included appendix vs. external repository is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of articles generally suitable
rubrics_metrics.description: The following types of articles are generally suitable: Research articles; Review papers; Case studies; Technical notes (e.g., new instrumentation or new analysis methods); Confirmatory studies; So-called ‘null’ results; Dataset description papers; Software papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your manuscript fits one of these categories, it is generally acceptable for EarthArXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software paper content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your EarthArXiv software paper should include a list of all authors and an explanation of the software's purpose, functionality, and domain of use at a level for a non-specialist reader. It should include references that include the software DOI and a link to the software archive, and mentions (where applicable) of projects using the software or publications enabled by the software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The software paper should not be solely documentation of API functionality. EarthArXiv follows software paper guidelines similar to the Journal of Open Source Software and recommends workflows that mint DOIs for code (e.g., GitHub+Zenodo). For peer review of software, consider venues such as JOSS or ROpenSci; for replications consider (Re)Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable: personal attacks, hateful or derogatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers reading as a personal attack, airing of grievances, or insulting to a group/class of people; racist and derogatory language will not be tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions will be rejected under the moderation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable: lack of citations to established scientific literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers without citations to established scientific literature (e.g., published, peer-reviewed articles or monographs; preprints intended for peer-reviewed publication; government reports; and publications from professional societies) will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your manuscript cites appropriate, established sources; preprints intended for peer-reviewed publication should include such citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable formats and content: commentaries/opinion pieces, posters, theses, course projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentaries and opinion pieces (i.e., an article that predominantly reflects the author’s opinion or beliefs) are not generally accepted (exceptions may be made for editorials or op-eds solicited by a particular journal). Posters and theses/course projects are not accepted; see alternatives (ESSOAr for posters, Thesis Commons for theses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work is primarily opinion or a course project, consider alternative venues or solicit editorial invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderators' judgment final and non-reviewable
rubrics_metrics.description: The moderator's judgement on the suitability of any material for EarthArXiv is final, requires no written justification, and is not reviewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure compliance with policies prior to submission since moderation decisions are final within EarthArXiv's process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation timing expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: When all submission requirements are met, EarthArXiv is typically able to moderate manuscripts within one week of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a guideline; time to publication can fluctuate due to interactions between EarthArXiv and authors, increases in submission rate, and volunteer moderator availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and hosting terms (DOI, hosting persistence, non-evaluation of quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon successfully completing moderation EarthArXiv agrees to publish your paper by assigning a DOI and providing free online hosting of your paper as long as EarthArXiv is operational. EarthArXiv is not a journal and does not evaluate the scientific quality of a paper. Once a paper passes moderation and is published, it persists on the system indefinitely. Yet, EarthArXiv reserves the right to remove papers after publication if fraud or plagiarism is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a DOI and persistent hosting, but understand that content can be removed for serious ethical breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy (viewed as retraction; reserved cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv views preprints as a form of publication. Every preprint receives a DOI making it citable and publicly available on the web. Withdrawals are viewed as retractions and reserved for special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of special cases include: significant errors/miscalculations where authors are unable to provide a revision, and confirmed cases of plagiarism and/or data fabrication. Withdrawal requests can be made via email to admin@eartharxiv.org and will be considered by the EarthArXiv Advisory Council on a case by case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: EarthArXiv will accept new PDFs in which a name change is applied to the author list, acknowledgments, and/or an email address. A name and email address can be changed in the author list metadata and in the submission history metadata for all existing versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for name changes can be made via email to admin@eartharxiv.org. EarthArXiv cannot make changes to other services or third-party tools that may display author lists harvested from EarthArXiv. Changing an author's name will not change the paper's DOI or version number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and plagiarism detection and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection of fraud and plagiarism involve manual moderation, automated algorithms, and community feedback. Any claim of fraud or plagiarism will be granted a review by the Advisory Board. Should the Board deem fraud or plagiarism to have occurred, the paper will be immediately removed from EarthArXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for manual and automated checks and community reporting; serious misconduct can lead to immediate removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibilities: copyright, journal policies, and co-author permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for determining if submitting to EarthArXiv precludes them from simultaneous or subsequent submission to their journal of choice. The submitting author must obtain permission from all co-authors prior to submission to EarthArXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EarthArXiv recommends Sherpa/Romeo as a starting point for publisher copyright policies but authors should check specific journal/publisher rules. Postprints will not be accepted if they are within the embargo period of the publishing journal. If EarthArXiv receives notice from a co-author that they did not authorize the publication, moderators will attempt to work with all authors to address the issue; if no agreement is reached, the preprint may be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: License
rubrics_metrics.description: This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 International License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By submitting, understand that content on EarthArXiv will be available under CC BY 2.0 unless otherwise stated by policy.
